item.title: Spicy Jerky for Heat Chasers
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Our seven hottest flavors, from sweet and spicy Mango Habanero to the double trouble of Hot Mamma Cheeto, with tips for climbing up to a 5.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. Every time we set up the booth, there's at least one person who walks straight past the Honey Teriyaki, looks my mom or dad in the eye and asks, "What's your hottest one?" I love those people. They're our heat chasers, and this post is for them.

If you're hunting for spicy jerky in Albuquerque, you're in the right place. New Mexico doesn't play around with chile, and neither do we. Below I'm walking through every flavor on our menu that sits at a 4 or a 5 on our heat scale, what makes each one different, and how to work your way up without scaring yourself off.

A quick word on our heat scale

Every Jerky Fixx flavor gets a number from 0 to 5. A 0 is no heat at all, like Salt, Garlic or Teriyaki. A 5 is as hot as we go. Out of our 25 flavors, four land at a 4 and three land at a 5. That's seven flavors built for people who want to feel it.

I already wrote a whole post ranking our green chile jerky flavors by heat, so if green chile is your thing, start there. This one covers the full spicy lineup, red, green and everything in between.

The 4s: hot, with personality

The 4s are where the menu gets fun. Each of these has real heat, but there's always a second flavor riding along with it.

Mango Habanero

Sweet mango up front, slow habanero burn on the way out. This is one of our top sellers, and I think it's because it tricks you a little. The first bite tastes like fruit. Then the habanero shows up and stays a while. If you like sweet heat, this is your flavor.

Takis

Rolled chile lime crunch flavor on thin cut carne seca. Sour, spicy and gone way too fast. Takis is another top seller, and it's a favorite with anyone who grew up with a bag of the real snack in their backpack. The lime keeps it bright, so the heat feels sharp instead of heavy.

Hot Cheetos

Red hot cheeto dust packed into every strip. Your fingers will be red and you won't care. It's one of our best sellers, and if you want the full story on how a snack aisle flavor ended up on our jerky, I covered it in Hot Cheeto jerky: yes, it is real.

Hot Mamma

A hot one for the heat chasers. Bold red chile spice with a serious kick. If the other 4s are flavor first and heat second, Hot Mamma flips that around. This is the one I point red chile fans toward when Red (a 3) isn't quite enough anymore.

The 5s: for the fiends

Now we're at the top of the scale. These three are the hottest things we make, and I mean that kindly when I say please respect them.

Hot Mamma Cheeto

Hot Mamma heat plus hot cheeto dust. Double trouble for spice fiends. Take everything from Hot Mamma, then add the cheeto dust on top. It's red, it's loud, and it's the one I see people dare each other to try at the table.

X-Hot Green

Our hottest green chile jerky. Green chile heat stacked on more green chile for the fiends who like it loud. X-Hot Green is one of our top sellers, which really says a lot about New Mexico. People here don't just put up with heat. They go looking for it.

X-Hot Green Chili Lime Salt

X-Hot green chile with lime and a hit of salt. Tangy, salty, very hot. Same top level heat as X-Hot Green, but with a sour, salty edge that makes it feel a little like a chile lime snack. If you love Takis and you want to go higher, this is a natural next step.

How to work your way up to a 5

Not everybody starts as a heat chaser. Some people become one. Here's how I'd climb if you're new to the hot end of the menu.

  1. Find your 3 first. Green, Red, X-Mas and Hot Cheeto Pickle all sit at a 3. If one of those feels comfortable, you're ready for a 4.
  2. Pick a 4 that matches a flavor you already like. Love sweet? Try Mango Habanero. Love chile lime snacks? Go with Takis. Love red chile? Hot Mamma.
  3. Grab a small bag before a large. A small bag is $7, so it's an easy way to test a new heat level without committing to a big bag.
  4. Keep a mild bag nearby. Having something like Garlic Parm or Honey Teriyaki on hand gives you a flavor break between hot bites.
  5. Then go for a 5. Pick the 5 that's closest to the 4 you liked. Takis fans usually lean toward X-Hot Green Chili Lime Salt. Hot Cheetos and Hot Mamma fans head for Hot Mamma Cheeto. Green chile people go straight to X-Hot Green.

And if you're feeding a group with mixed heat tolerance, my game day flavor guide has ideas for mixing mild and hot bags so everybody's happy.

Build your own heat flight

One of my favorite ways to try the spicy side of the menu is to make a little heat flight. Grab a few small bags at different levels, maybe a 3, a 4 and a 5, and taste them in order with friends. It turns snack time into a game, and you find out pretty quickly who the real fiends are in your group.

You can see every flavor and its heat number on the menu. A small bag is $7 and a large bag is $20. Add what you want to your cart and send the order. The crew texts you to confirm, our dealer drops it at your door, and you get a photo once it's delivered. We take Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash.

Try the heat in person

Want to taste before you buy? We set up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho, and the spicy flavors are always a big part of the conversation at our table. Stay tuned for upcoming events, and check the dealer locator to sign up for event alerts so you know where we'll be next. You can also follow along on Instagram and Facebook.

So, heat chasers, which one is your go to? Text us at 505-922-5683 or 505-364-0678 and tell us your favorite 5. I promise my family wants to know.

item.title: Green Chile Jerky Flavors Ranked by Heat
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: We make seven green chile jerky flavors. Here they are ranked from mellow to "bring a drink," with tips on where to start and how to work your way up.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. Green chile is kind of our love language at Jerky Fixx. It shows up in so many of our flavors that people at the booth sometimes ask me, "Okay, but which green one should I get?" Fair question. We have seven of them, and they are not all the same kind of hot.

So today I'm lining up every green chile jerky flavor we make and ranking them by heat, from the gentle ones up to the ones my family saves for the true fiends. If you want the bigger picture of red, green and Christmas, I already covered that in New Mexico jerky and green chile carne seca. This post is all about the heat ladder.

How our heat scale works

Every flavor on our menu gets a heat number from 0 to 5. A 0 means no heat at all, like Salt or Honey Teriyaki. A 5 is as hot as we go. Our green chile flavors start at a 2 and climb all the way to the top, which makes them a great way to find out where your comfort zone is.

One thing to know up front: there's no green chile flavor at a 4. The ladder goes 2, then 3, then a big jump to 5. I'll come back to that, because it matters if you're working your way up.

All of these are our small batch carne seca, thin cut beef with a heavy hand on the seasoning and a long, slow dry. If you're curious about the process, I wrote a plain English guide to carne seca.

Heat 2: the easy starters

Green Chili Ranch

Cool ranch seasoning with a mellow green chile warmth. This is the one I hand to people who say they "don't really do spicy." The ranch keeps everything smooth and familiar, and the green chile just sort of hums in the background. You get the flavor of green chile without the sweat.

Grab it if: you want green chile flavor first and heat second.

Honey Teriyaki Green

Sweet honey teriyaki with a little green chile bite on the finish. Honey Teriyaki on its own is one of our top sellers and a big favorite with kids and grandmas, so this one is like its slightly braver cousin. It starts sweet, then the chile shows up at the end to say hi.

Grab it if: you love sweet and savory and want to dip a toe into heat.

Heat 3: the real New Mexico middle

This is where a lot of New Mexicans feel right at home.

Green

Classic New Mexico green chile carne seca. Earthy, bright and just the right burn. If you only try one green chile jerky from us, make it this one. It's the flavor the rest of the green lineup is built on.

Grab it if: you want the classic.

Lemon Pepper Green

Zesty lemon pepper meets green chile heat. Bright, peppery and hard to put down. Our regular Lemon Pepper is a 1 and one of our top sellers, so this is how you take a flavor people already love and turn it up two notches. The lemon keeps it fresh, which makes the heat feel lighter than you'd expect.

Grab it if: you like a zesty, peppery snack with real kick.

Garlic Parm Green

Savory garlic and parmesan with a green chile kick. Garlic Parm is another top seller, and at a 0 it's one of our mildest. Adding green chile turns it into something rich and savory with a warm finish.

Grab it if: you're a garlic person who wants some heat along for the ride.

Heat 5: for the fiends

Here's that jump I mentioned. There's no green 4, so going from a 3 to a 5 is a real leap. Please respect it.

X-Hot Green

Our hottest green chile jerky. Green chile heat stacked on more green chile for the fiends who like it loud. It's also one of our top sellers, which tells you a lot about New Mexico. People here don't just tolerate heat, they chase it.

Grab it if: Green feels too comfortable and you want the full blast.

X-Hot Green Chili Lime Salt

X-Hot green chile with lime and a hit of salt. Tangy, salty, very hot. Same fire as X-Hot Green with a bright, sour edge. Same heat level, different personality.

Grab it if: you love chile, lime and salt together and you're not scared.

How to climb the ladder

If you want to work your way up, here's how I'd do it:

  1. Start at a 2. Green Chili Ranch or Honey Teriyaki Green.
  2. Move to Green. It's the true benchmark. If it feels good, you're ready for more.
  3. Play around at 3. Try Lemon Pepper Green and Garlic Parm Green to see how different flavors carry the same heat.
  4. Only then try a 5. Start with a small bag of X-Hot Green before you commit to a large.

Since there's no green 4, you can borrow a stepping stone from the rest of the menu. Mango Habanero, Hot Cheetos and Takis are all 4s, so one of those is a smart way to test the waters before the X-Hot greens.

Order your green chile jerky

You can find every flavor and its heat level on the menu. A small bag is $7 and a large bag is $20, so a small bag at a few different heat levels is an easy way to build your own taste test. Add what you want to your cart and send the order. The crew texts you to confirm, our dealer drops it at your door, and you get a photo once it's delivered. We take Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash.

Want to try before you buy? We set up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho. Stay tuned for upcoming events, and check the dealer locator for event alerts so you know where we'll be next. You can also follow along on Instagram.

If you're putting together snacks for a crowd, my game day flavor guide has ideas for mixing mild and hot bags.

So where do you land on the ladder? Text us at 505-922-5683 and tell us your number. We love hearing which green you picked.

item.title: Hot Cheeto Jerky: Yes, It Is Real
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Yes, Hot Cheeto jerky is a real thing, and it's one of our best sellers. Here's what Hot Cheetos and Hot Cheeto Pickle taste like and who should grab which bag.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. If you've ever scrolled our menu, seen the words Hot Cheeto jerky and thought, "Wait, is that real?" this post is for you.

Yes. It's real. It's on our menu, it's one of our top sellers, and it has a sibling that sounds even wilder. So today I want to give these flavors the spotlight they deserve and help you figure out which one belongs in your bag.

The short version

We make two flavors built around that red Hot Cheeto dust:

  • Hot Cheetos sits at a 4 on our heat scale.
  • Hot Cheeto Pickle sits at a 3.

There's also a third member of the family, Hot Mamma Cheeto, which is a 5. My mom gets the credit for that one, and I already told the whole story in Hot Mamma Cheeto and flavors made for Burque. So this post is about the other two, the two that make people look twice at the menu.

Why Hot Cheetos on jerky even makes sense

If you grew up around here, you probably don't need convincing. Hot Cheetos with lime after school is basically a New Mexico food group. Chile goes on everything here, and we love snacks that are sweet, sour, salty and spicy all in one bite.

Our base is always the same: small batch carne seca, which is thin cut beef with a heavy hand on the seasoning and a long, slow dry. That thin cut is the secret here. Thin strips grab onto seasoning, so a dust like Hot Cheeto really coats every piece instead of sliding off. If you want the full breakdown of how carne seca is made, I wrote a plain English guide to carne seca earlier this week.

So when people say Hot Cheeto jerky sounds like a gimmick, I get it. But it comes from the same place as our green chile flavors. We take what people here already love and put it on beef.

Hot Cheetos: heat level 4

Here's how we describe it on the menu: red hot Cheeto dust packed into every strip. Your fingers will be red and you won't care.

That pretty much sums it up. This is the flavor for the person who always has a bag of Hot Cheetos in the car, the backpack or the desk drawer. It's bold, it's spicy and it's red. Very red. Keep a napkin nearby, or don't, and just own the red fingertips like everyone else at the booth.

At a 4, it's a real step up from our mild flavors. It's not our hottest, but it's not shy either. If Green at a 3 feels comfortable to you, Hot Cheetos is a fun next step.

Who it's for: Hot Cheeto fans, spice lovers who aren't ready for a 5 yet, and anyone who wants a snack that starts a conversation.

Hot Cheeto Pickle: heat level 3

This is the one that gets the biggest double take. The menu says it best: dill pickle tang meets Hot Cheeto heat. It sounds wild. It sells out anyway.

The pickle is what makes it work. Heat needs something to play against, and that sour dill tang cuts right through the spice, so every bite is salty, sour and hot at the same time. If you've ever eaten a pickle and a bag of Hot Cheetos together from the corner store, you already know this combo. We just put it on carne seca.

It also comes in a notch milder than straight Hot Cheetos, at a 3, so it's a friendly place to start if you're curious about the Cheeto flavors but nervous about the heat.

Who it's for: Pickle people, sour snack fans, and anyone who likes the idea of Hot Cheeto jerky but wants a little less fire.

And if you love the pickle part most, we also make plain Pickle at a 1. Tangy dill pickle jerky, sour, salty and weirdly addictive.

Which one should you grab?

Here's how I'd pick:

  1. New to spicy jerky? Start with Hot Cheeto Pickle. The tang balances the heat.
  2. Hot Cheeto loyalist? Go straight to Hot Cheetos. It's the classic.
  3. Can't decide? Get one of each. A small bag is $7, so trying both is easy.
  4. Already eat a 4 for breakfast? Hot Mamma Cheeto is waiting for you at a 5. You've been warned.

If snack aisle flavors are your thing, Takis is another fun one at a 4, with rolled chile lime crunch flavor on thin cut carne seca. A Hot Cheetos and Takis combo is a strong move for a game day snack bag.

One quick note: everything we make contains beef, and some flavors contain dairy, soy, wheat or corn. If that matters for you or someone you're sharing with, text us before you order and ask about the flavor you want.

How to get Hot Cheeto jerky in Albuquerque

The easiest way is right from your phone. Find Hot Cheetos and Hot Cheeto Pickle on the menu, add them to your cart and send your order. A small bag is $7 and a large bag is $20. The crew texts you to confirm, our dealer drops it at your door, and you get a photo once it's delivered. You can pay with Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash.

You can also text or call 505-922-5683 or 505-364-0678, or email jerkyfixx@gmail.com if you have a question first.

If you'd rather taste it in person, we set up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho. Our last stop was New Mexico Jerky Fest, Halloween Edition, on October 31, 2026 at Isleta Resort and Casino. Stay tuned for upcoming events. Check the dealer locator and sign up for alerts, or follow us on Instagram so you hear about the next one.

So yes, Hot Cheeto jerky is real, and Jerky Fixx makes it in small batches right here in New Mexico. The only real question left is whether you're a straight Hot Cheetos person or a pickle person. Either way, we've got a bag for you.

item.title: What Is Carne Seca? A Plain English Guide
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Is carne seca the same thing as jerky? Here is the plain English answer, how we make ours in Albuquerque and an easy way to pick your first bag.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. You'll see the words carne seca all over this website, and I realized we never stopped to explain them. If you've ever looked at our menu and wondered what carne seca actually is, but felt weird asking, this one's for you.

I'll keep it simple. No food science, just the plain English version.

The short answer

Carne seca is Spanish for "dried meat." At Jerky Fixx, that means dried, seasoned beef.

So is carne seca the same as jerky? Pretty much, yes. Both are dried, seasoned beef. Carne seca is the traditional New Mexico name for it, and it's a name people here feel at home with. You'll see us use both words all over this site, and that isn't an accident. Some people are looking for jerky in Albuquerque, some are looking for carne seca, and we want everybody to end up in the same happy place.

Then why use two names?

Mostly because of where you are. "Jerky" is the word you'll hear just about everywhere. "Carne seca" is the name with roots here in New Mexico, so it carries a lot of home feeling with it.

When we call ours carne seca, we're also telling you what kind of snack to expect. Ours is small batch, chile forward and thin cut, and every bag comes from the same family crew you'll meet at our booth. Not every bag that says jerky can say that, and that's the part I care about most.

How we make ours

You don't have to take my word for it, because the whole process is on our Lab page, video and all. Here's the quick version, using a lemon pepper and green chile batch as the example:

  1. Slice. The beef gets cut thin, to about 1/8 inch.
  2. Lay out. The strips go out on the drying racks.
  3. Season. The seasoning goes on heavy. This is not the step where we hold back.
  4. Chile. New Mexico green chile goes on top.
  5. Dry. The racks go into the dehydrator.
  6. Low and slow. The batch is held at 150°F until it's done.
  7. Bag it. Done means ready to bag, and then it's ready for you.

That's the whole method in one line: thin cut beef, a heavy hand with the seasoning and a long, slow dry. What changes from batch to batch is the flavor we stack on top.

What it tastes like

This is where "dried meat" stops being a helpful description, because carne seca tastes like whatever you season it with. Ours runs from simple to very loud. We have 25 flavors, and each one gets a heat number from 0 to 5.

If you want to taste the beef itself, Salt is the purest way to do it. It's simple, beefy and clean, just meat and salt, with a 0 on the heat scale. Green is the New Mexico classic, earthy and bright with the right burn, and it sits at a 3. And then there's the fun end of the menu, like Takis at a 4, which is rolled chile lime crunch flavor on thin cut carne seca. Same base, totally different snack.

I went deeper on chile in my guide to New Mexico jerky and green chile carne seca, and on how we dream up the wild ones in our flavor engineering post.

Your first bag

If carne seca is new to you, here's an easy way to start, based on how much heat you like:

  • No heat, please: Honey Teriyaki is sweet, sticky and savory, and it's a 0. It's our gateway flavor for the kids and the grandmas. Garlic Parm is also a 0 and one of our top sellers.
  • A little warmth: Lemon Pepper is a 1 and a classic. Green Chili Ranch is a 2 with a mellow green chile warmth.
  • Real New Mexico heat: Green, Red and X-Mas are all 3s. X-Mas is red and green chile together, for when you can't choose.
  • Bring it on: X-Hot Green is a 5 and our hottest green chile jerky. You've been warned, and you probably won't listen, which is fine by us.

One thing worth knowing before you order: everything contains beef, and some flavors contain dairy, soy, wheat or corn. If that matters for you or someone you're sharing with, text us and ask about the flavor you're eyeing.

Where to find carne seca in Albuquerque

The easiest way to try it is right from your phone. Browse all 25 flavors on the menu, add what you want to your cart and send your order. A small bag is $7 and a large bag is $20. The crew texts you to confirm, the dealer drops it at your door and you get a photo once it's delivered. You can pay with Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash.

If you'd rather try it in person, we set up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho. Our last stop was New Mexico Jerky Fest, Halloween Edition, on October 31, 2026 at Isleta Resort and Casino. Stay tuned for upcoming events. You can follow us on Instagram or check the dealer locator and sign up for alerts so you hear about the next one. For more on your options, read where to buy jerky in Albuquerque.

So that's carne seca. Dried, seasoned beef with a New Mexico name, made by my family one small batch at a time. Now you can skip the guessing and go straight to the fun question: how hot do you want it?

item.title: Jerky Fest 2026 Recap: Halloween at Isleta
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Costumes, candy, a glowing LED flavor board and a whole lot of carne seca. Here is how the 4th annual New Mexico Jerky Fest went down at Isleta.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. We're still recovering, but in the best way. On Halloween night, Saturday, October 31, my family brought Jerky Fixx to the 4th annual New Mexico Jerky Fest at Isleta Resort and Casino, and the energy was honestly insane. If you came by the booth, thank you. If you missed it, here's the recap.

A Halloween edition of Jerky Fest

This year's Jerky Fest had a Halloween theme, and people went all in. We saw full costumes, face paint, matching crews and kids dragging their parents from table to table. My parents, Joseph and Sabrina, rocked matching pinstripe Jerky Fixx jerseys with face paint to match. The booth had pink, purple and black balloons, spiderwebs, a skull chalkboard that says "God provides, we prepare, you enjoy" and a bowl of candy for the trick or treaters.

Our two bull skull trophies from past Jerky Fests made the trip too, front and center on the table.

A flavor board that lit up the room

The biggest upgrade this year was our flavor board. DSI, Document Solutions, Inc. sponsored the Jerky Fixx booth with one of their dynamic LED digital signage displays, and it stopped people in their tracks. It showed all 25 flavors, from X-Hot Green down to Tajin Limon, with our bag prices and how to pay.

DSI's marketing specialist, Toni Torivio, made the animated slideshows that ran on it. They were bright, loud and full of color, which is exactly how our carne seca tastes. Watching people stand in front of it and point at the flavors they wanted was one of my favorite parts of the night.

The display also had a QR code, so anyone could scan it and land right on our brand new website, built by DYAD Marketects. If that's how you found this page, welcome. You can browse the full menu, save your favorites and order whenever the craving hits.

Why a sign like that matters for a small business

For a family business like ours, a booth is everything. You've got a few seconds while people walk past to show them who you are. A glowing sign that cycles through every flavor does that job for you, and it answers the first two questions everybody asks: what flavors do you have, and how much is a bag. It also meant my parents could spend less time reading the menu out loud and more time handing out samples and talking with people. Seeing our roadrunner logo and lightning animated that big was pretty special for our whole family.

What people kept asking for

We sampled a lot of carne seca. The heat chasers went straight for X-Hot Green and Hot Cheetos, the families loved Honey Teriyaki and Garlic Parm, and Hot Cheeto Pickle got the usual "wait, pickle?" right before people bought a bag anyway. A lot of folks also met our spiciest new mix, Hot Mamma Cheeto, for the first time. I wrote more about how we come up with flavors like that in our flavor engineering post.

Thank you, Burque

Events like Jerky Fest are why we do this. Jerky Fest always feels like a family reunion with way more jerky, and we loved seeing so many returning faces next to brand new fiends. Thank you to everyone who stopped by, tried a sample, took a picture in their costume or told us about their favorite flavor. Thank you to the Jerky Fest team and Isleta Resort and Casino for hosting, and a huge thank you to DSI and Toni for making our booth glow.

Where to find us next

Jerky Fest is a wrap, so stay tuned for upcoming events. Follow us on Instagram and Facebook, or check the dealer locator for our next stop. Can't wait that long? Small bags are $7 and large bags are $20, and you can order direct for door drop off around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho.

item.title: Hot Mamma Cheeto and Flavors Made for Burque
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Burqueños eat chile on everything, so our flavors have to keep up. Here is how we build them, and the story behind Hot Mamma Cheeto.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah. People always ask how we come up with 25 flavors. The honest answer is that we make jerky for Burqueños, and Burqueños have a very specific palate. So today I'm pulling back the curtain on how we build flavors, and I get to introduce one my mom is really proud of: Hot Mamma Cheeto.

Cooking for the Burque palate

If you grew up in Albuquerque, you already know the rules. Chile goes on everything. "Red or green?" is a real question, and "Christmas" is a real answer. You probably had Takis or Hot Cheetos with lime after school, a pickle from the corner store and Tajin on your mango. Sweet, sour, salty and spicy all in one bite is just normal here.

It goes beyond snacks, too. Think about a plate of enchiladas smothered in green, a bowl of posole with red chile on the side, or roasted chile in the air every fall when the roasters fire up outside the grocery stores. Food here is bold and it's personal. Everybody has a favorite spot, a favorite heat and strong opinions about both.

That's the palate we cook for. Our base is always the same: small batch carne seca, thin cut beef, a heavy hand on the seasoning and a long, slow dry. What changes is how we stack flavors on top of it.

How we engineer a flavor

We don't have a lab coat, but we do have a process.

  1. Start with what Burque already loves. Green chile, red chile, lime, garlic, Hot Cheetos, pickles and Tajin all come straight from the snacks people grew up on.
  2. Pick a heat level on purpose. Every flavor gets a number from 0 to 5, so a Honey Teriyaki fan and an X-Hot Green fiend can both find their bag.
  3. Balance the bite. Heat needs something to play against. That's why you'll see lime with chile, dill with Hot Cheeto and honey with teriyaki.
  4. Make it crunch and cling. Thin cut carne seca holds onto seasoning, so dusts like Hot Cheeto and Takis really coat every strip.
  5. Test it on family and customers. If people at the booth keep coming back for another sample, it earns a spot on the menu.

That's how you end up with flavors like X-Mas (red and green chile together), Tajin Limon, Takis and Hot Cheeto Pickle. Some of them sound wild on paper. They sell out anyway.

Meet Hot Mamma Cheeto

Hot Mamma Cheeto is what happens when you take two fan favorites and turn them up. Hot Mamma is our bold red chile flavor with a serious kick. Hot Cheetos is red hot Cheeto dust packed into every strip. Put them together and you get Hot Mamma Cheeto, sitting at heat level 5, right up there with X-Hot Green.

It's double trouble for spice fiends: deep red chile heat first, then that Hot Cheeto crunch and tang that keeps you reaching back into the bag. My mom, Sabrina, is the Hot Mamma behind it, so here she is to introduce it herself.

A lot of people tried it for the first time at Jerky Fest, and it went fast. If you like Hot Cheetos and Hot Mamma, this is your bag. If you're new to our heat scale, maybe start with Hot Cheetos (4) and work your way up.

Why small batch matters for bold flavors

Big brands have to make one flavor taste the same in every state. We don't. Because we make small batches here in Albuquerque, we can season heavy, tweak a recipe when customers tell us what they want, and keep a flavor that only makes sense to people from here. That's also why we can say yes to custom requests. If there's a combo you've been dreaming about, ask us at the next event or send us a message.

Which flavor fits your Burque taste?

  • Green chile purist? Try Green, then X-Hot Green when you're ready.
  • Can't choose? X-Mas gives you red and green together.
  • Snack aisle kid at heart? Hot Cheetos, Takis and Hot Cheeto Pickle.
  • Chasing the burn? Hot Mamma Cheeto. You've been warned.
  • Keeping it mellow? Honey Teriyaki and Garlic Parm.

item.title: The Best Jerky Flavors for Game Day
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Mild, medium or straight up X-Hot. Here is how to build a game day jerky bag from our flavors so everybody on the couch or in the bleachers finds a favorite.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, it's Aaliyah again. If you have ever seen our booth at a ball game, you already know game day and jerky go together. People walk up between innings with their kids, their friends and their whole crew, and the first question is almost always the same: "Which one should we get?" With 25 flavors on the table, I get it. So I put this guide together for anyone building a game day snack bag, whether you're watching from the bleachers or from your living room.

Why jerky works on game day

Game day snacks have a few jobs. They need to be easy to pass around, they can't make a mess of the couch (well, mostly), and they have to keep people happy through a close game. Jerky checks all of those boxes. You can open a bag, hand out strips and nobody needs a plate.

Ours is small batch carne seca, made by my family here in Albuquerque with thin cut beef, a heavy hand on the seasoning and a long, slow dry. That thin cut makes it easy to share, and the seasoning means every strip actually tastes like something.

Know the heat scale first

Every flavor on our menu has a heat level from 0 to 5. Here's the quick way I think about it for a group:

  • 0 to 1 is for everyone, including the kids and anyone who says "no spice, please."
  • 2 to 3 is a friendly warm up. You'll feel it, but it won't take over.
  • 4 is hot. This is for the people who put chile on everything.
  • 5 is for the fiends. Seriously.

A good game day bag usually covers at least two of these ranges, so nobody gets left out.

The crowd pleasers (heat 0 to 1)

If you're feeding a mixed group, start here. These are the flavors that disappear first when kids are around.

  • Honey Teriyaki (0) is sweet, sticky and savory. It's our gateway flavor for the kids and the grandmas, and it's one of our top sellers.
  • Garlic Parm (0) brings roasted garlic and nutty parmesan. Mellow on the heat, loud on the flavor. Another top seller.
  • Teriyaki (0) gives you a savory teriyaki glaze on tender, thin cut beef.
  • Salt (0) is simple and beefy for the purists in the group.
  • Lemon Pepper (1) is bright lemon and cracked black pepper, a classic that never gets old.
  • Salt x Pepper (1) is the classic pair, and it's hard to argue with.

The middle of the lineup (heat 2 to 3)

This is where New Mexico really shows up. If your crew grew up on chile, these are a safe bet.

  • Green (3) is our classic New Mexico green chile carne seca. Earthy, bright and just the right burn.
  • Red (3) has deep, smoky red chile flavor.
  • X-Mas (3) is red and green together, Christmas style, for the people who can't choose.
  • Green Chili Ranch (2) is cool ranch seasoning with a mellow green chile warmth. Ranch and game day? Come on.
  • Tajin Limon (2) has that chile lime seasoning with a bright limon finish.
  • Hot Cheeto Pickle (3) is dill pickle tang meeting hot cheeto heat. It sounds wild, and it sells out anyway.

If you want more on our chile flavors, my post on New Mexico jerky and green chile carne seca goes deeper.

The snack aisle favorites (heat 4)

Some of our most fun flavors are inspired by the snacks you'd already grab on game day.

  • Hot Cheetos (4) packs red hot cheeto dust into every strip. Your fingers will be red and you won't care.
  • Takis (4) brings rolled chile lime crunch flavor to thin cut carne seca. Sour, spicy and gone way too fast.
  • Mango Habanero (4) is sweet mango up front and a slow habanero burn on the way out.

All three of these are top sellers, which tells you something about how much people love a little heat with their game.

For the heat chasers (heat 5)

Every group has that one person. You know the one. These are for them.

  • X-Hot Green (5) is our hottest green chile jerky, green chile stacked on more green chile. It's also one of our top sellers.
  • Hot Mamma Cheeto (5) is Hot Mamma heat plus hot cheeto dust. Double trouble.
  • X-Hot Green Chili Lime Salt (5) is tangy, salty and very hot.

Have a drink nearby. I'm just saying.

Three easy game day bags

Not sure how to mix it? Here are a few combos I like to suggest at the booth:

  1. The family section: Honey Teriyaki, Garlic Parm and Lemon Pepper. Zero to low heat, big flavor, happy kids.
  2. The New Mexico watch party: Green, Red and X-Mas, plus Green Chili Ranch for anyone who wants it a little softer.
  3. The heat check: Hot Cheetos, Takis, Mango Habanero and one bag of X-Hot Green to see who taps out first.

Small bags are $7 and large bags are $20. For a bigger group, a couple of large bags of the crowd pleasers plus a few smalls of the hot ones is a nice way to cover everyone without overbuying the spicy stuff.

How to get it before kickoff

If you're hosting, the easiest move is to order ahead. Pick your flavors, add them to your cart and send the order in. Someone from the crew texts to confirm, you pay with Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash, and our dealer drops the order at your door and sends a photo once it's delivered. You can also text or call 505-922-5683 or 505-364-0678 with questions.

If you'd rather grab it in person, we show up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho. Check the dealer locator to see where we're posting up next. Our last stop was Jerky Fest at Isleta Resort and Casino on Oct 31, 2026. Stay tuned for upcoming events, and follow us on Instagram to hear first.

For more ways to find us, my post on where to buy jerky in Albuquerque lays it all out.

See you at the game

Whether your crew is all about Honey Teriyaki or daring each other to try X-Hot Green, there's a Jerky Fixx flavor for every seat in the house. Thanks for supporting my family's small business, and good luck to your team. Unless they're playing mine.

item.title: New Mexico Jerky and Green Chile Carne Seca
item.dc:creator: Aaliyah Penn
item.description: Green chile, red chile and a little Christmas style. Here is what makes New Mexico jerky its own thing, and which Jerky Fixx flavors to try first.
item.content:encoded:
Hi again, it's Aaliyah. People who aren't from here sometimes ask me what makes New Mexico jerky different from the stuff you can grab anywhere. I grew up with the answer, but I had to stop and think about how to explain it. The short version is chile. The longer version is chile, tradition and a family that likes to have fun with flavor.

What carne seca means here

Jerky and carne seca are both dried, seasoned beef. In New Mexico, carne seca is the traditional name, and it carries a lot of home feeling with it. When we say we make small batch carne seca, we mean thin cut beef, a heavy hand with the seasoning and a long, slow dry. Nothing fancy, just done carefully, and done by hand by the same crew you meet at our booth.

A lot of what you see on store shelves leans on one or two safe flavors. New Mexico jerky tends to lean on chile, and once you've had it that way, plain can feel like it's missing something.

Green chile jerky, the New Mexico classic

If you ask me what jerky nm lovers should try first, it's green chile. Our Green is classic New Mexico green chile carne seca. It's earthy and bright, with just the right burn. It sits around a 3 on our 0 to 5 heat scale, so it has a real kick without being scary.

Green chile shows up all over our menu, because we can't stop ourselves:

  • Green is the classic. Earthy, bright, the right burn.
  • Lemon Pepper Green mixes zesty lemon pepper with green chile heat.
  • Garlic Parm Green is savory garlic and parmesan with a green chile kick.
  • Honey Teriyaki Green is sweet honey teriyaki with a little green chile bite on the finish.
  • Green Chili Ranch is cool ranch seasoning with a mellow green chile warmth. This is a good one if you want the chile flavor without much fire.
  • X-Hot Green is our hottest green chile jerky. It's green chile heat stacked on more green chile, and it's one of our top sellers.
  • X-Hot Green Chili Lime Salt takes that X-Hot green chile and adds lime and a hit of salt. Tangy, salty and very hot.

So if you're searching for green chile jerky, you have a whole range to work with, from mellow to "bring a drink."

Red, green or Christmas

Anybody from New Mexico knows the question: red or green? Our Red is red chile beef jerky with deep, smoky New Mexico red chile flavor. And if you can't pick, we have you covered. X-Mas is red and green chile together, Christmas style, the way New Mexico does it. It's a 3 on the heat scale, and it saves you from a hard decision.

The fun side of New Mexico jerky

Here's where my family likes to play. We grew up on chile, but we also grew up on snack aisle favorites, so a bunch of our flavors borrow from those:

  • Hot Cheetos has red hot cheeto dust packed into every strip.
  • Hot Cheeto Pickle is dill pickle tang meets hot cheeto heat.
  • Takis brings rolled chile lime crunch flavor to thin cut carne seca.
  • Tajin Limon is chile lime Tajin style seasoning with a bright limon finish.
  • Mango Habanero is sweet mango up front with a slow habanero burn.
  • Asian Zing is savory, tangy and a little sweet.

That playful streak got noticed. We won Most Exotic Flavor at New Mexico Jerky Fest, and we also took home Best Booth. Honestly, that tells you a lot about us. We take the food seriously, and we also think a pickle and hot cheeto jerky is a great idea.

Not everything has to be hot

I don't want anyone to think they need a cast iron stomach. Plenty of our flavors have no heat or very little. Salt, Garlic, Garlic Parm, Teriyaki and Honey Teriyaki are all a 0. Salt x Pepper, Lemon Pepper and Pickle sit at a 1. These are great for kids, for picky eaters and for anyone who wants New Mexico jerky without the burn.

A good trick for a first order is to pick one mild bag, one medium chile bag like Green or Red, and one wild card. Then you can see where your taste lands.

How to try it

You can order from the full menu, where every flavor has its heat level and description. A small bag is $7 and a large bag is $20. Send your order from the cart page or the contact form, and we'll text you to confirm. You can pay with Cash App, Venmo, Apple Pay or cash, and the dealer drops it at your door and sends a photo once it's delivered.

Prefer to taste first? Catch us at a pop up or festival. Our last one was New Mexico Jerky Fest, Halloween Edition, at Isleta Resort and Casino on October 31, 2026. Stay tuned for upcoming events, and sign up for event alerts on the dealer locator so you don't miss the next chance to sample.

Keep exploring

If you're in town and want the practical side, read where to buy jerky in Albuquerque. And if you want to know who is behind all this chile, meet the family.

Green, red or Christmas, I hope you find your flavor. Text us and tell us which one you picked. We love hearing it.

item.title: Meet the Jerky Fixx Family

item.description: Joseph Garduno, Sabrina Penn Garduno and the crew. Meet the family behind Jerky Fixx, small batch jerky and carne seca from Albuquerque.
item.content:encoded:
Hi, I'm Aaliyah Penn, and this is my favorite post to write. Jerky Fixx is my family's business, and I get to be the one who tells you who we are. Some people search for us as "Jerky Fix," and that's totally fine. You found us either way.

Made with love, faith and family

Our little motto says it all: made with love, faith and family. Jerky Fixx is a family operation out of Albuquerque, New Mexico. It's run by my dad, Joseph Garduno, and my mom, Sabrina Penn Garduno, along with the rest of the crew. Every batch gets cut, seasoned and dried by the same people you meet at the booth.

We started making carne seca for the people we love, and the people we love kept asking for more. Now there are 25 flavors, and a lot of folks around the 505 who can't quit.

Joseph Garduno and Sabrina Penn Garduno

My parents are Jerky Fixx. Joseph and Sabrina are husband and wife, and it all comes down to good food, fun flavors and feeding people they care about. You'll usually find them behind the table at pop ups, festivals and softball games, handing out samples and talking flavor with whoever walks up.

I don't want to put words in their mouths, so I'll just say what I see. They care about doing it right, they care about the folks who buy a bag and they care about doing it as a family. If you stop by the booth and tell them which flavor you loved, they will light up.

The crew at the table

Every batch gets cut, seasoned and dried by the same crew that shows up at events. That means you'll see familiar faces if you come around more than once.

We also have what we call the dealer. That's the person who brings your order to your door when you order online. Once it's dropped off, the dealer sends a photo so you know it arrived. It's a small thing, but it makes ordering from us feel like getting a package from a friend.

And then there's me

I'm Aaliyah Penn, Joseph and Sabrina's daughter. I'm studying web design, and I manage and maintain this website. That means I update the flavors, post the next event, watch the order forms and write these blog posts. It's a real-life class project that my family happens to eat. You can read a bit more about me on my author page.

Having a family business and a web design major under one roof is a great combination. My parents bring the flavors, and I try to make it easy for you to find them.

What we make

We make small batch beef jerky and carne seca, and our approach is simple: thin cut beef, a heavy hand with the seasoning and a long, slow dry. Our menu has 25 flavors, and the heat scale runs from 0 to 5.

Some of our top sellers are:

  • X-Hot Green, our hottest green chile jerky
  • Hot Cheetos, Takis and Hot Cheeto Pickle, for snack lovers
  • Garlic Parm, Honey Teriyaki and Lemon Pepper, for easy crowd pleasers
  • Mango Habanero, sweet up front with a slow burn

Want to see the whole list? The full menu has every flavor with its heat level. For the chile story, read our post on New Mexico jerky and green chile carne seca.

The hardware

Our family got a nice surprise at New Mexico Jerky Fest, where we won Most Exotic Flavor and Best Booth. We still can't believe it sometimes. The trophies sit proudly in our photos, and they remind us why we do this. We're heading back this Saturday, October 31, 2026, for the Halloween Edition at Isleta Resort & Casino. Come say hi, try a sample and see the booth in person.

Where to find us

We show up at pop ups, festivals and ball games around Albuquerque and Rio Rancho. If you want to know what's next, the dealer locator on the home page has our next stop, and you can sign up for dealer alerts. Need the practical details? Say hi

You can text or call 505-922-5683 or 505-364-0678, or email jerkyfixx@gmail.com. We're also on Instagram, Facebook and Threads. A real person from the family writes back.

Thank you for letting us be part of your snack time. It means everything to a small family business.
